text:
Marketing slides claim on-device AI will replace cloud APIs tomorrow, but your phone operating system does not care about your LLM.

If your app gets killed in the background because a small model ate 1.5GB of RAM, the user experience is dead on arrival. 📱

I spent part of last week trying to embed a quantized 2B parameter model inside a mobile app using ONNX Runtime. On paper, a 1.2GB memory footprint sounds like a fair trade for zero latency and complete privacy. In practice, mobile memory managers are unforgiving.

When an iOS or Android device hits thermal limits or memory pressure, the OS does not politely ask your model to pause. It silently kills your process. Loading model weights onto the GPU heats up the device, which dims the screen and throttles CPU clock speeds within minutes of continuous inference. 📉

The real challenge of edge AI is not quantization accuracy loss. It is thermal management and memory limits.

Mobile AI will not be built by squeezing massive foundation models onto handheld chips. It will be built through tiny, hyper-specialized micro-models that handle instant local classification, leaving context-heavy reasoning to hybrid edge-cloud pipelines.

Are you seeing your teams push for full local execution, or is a hybrid edge-cloud setup winning in your production apps? 🤔
